content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes near historical highs often trigger model overcorrection, leading to premature price declines.", "Models exhibit mean-reversion bias in low-sentiment periods, underestimating sustained price declines.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price momentum, particularly in upward trends.", "Models lag behind true price movements during sharp reversals, especially when sentiment shifts abruptly.", "High sentiment volatility correlates with forecast instability, particularly in mid-cycle price corrections.", "Forecast bias is strongest when historical price trends are volatile and sentiment is mixed.", "Sentiment-driven momentum often overrides model forecasts in late-cycle price surges."]}
